_doc: 1.12.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T2b, 2026-08-17) — the open is authored
per seat and the 3-bet multiplier gains two more rungs. Before this change
the pack opened 3.0bb with share 1.000 from all eight opening seats, 741
times per 4,000 hands — the second highest volume on the table, so this is
where seat-blind sizing was most visible.
It takes the small size more often than either other regular at every seat
(0.14 early against the tag's 0.12 and the nit's 0.10; 0.85 late against
0.80 and 0.62), and its mean open is the lowest of the three. That is the
archetype rather than a free choice: a LAG's edge comes from opening a wide
range cheaply. A first draft claimed exactly this and authored the reverse,
which is why the ordering is now stated as numbers.
The seat ladder and the small-blind bump are the tag's; see its 1.10.0
entry.
Every rung is on the 0.5bb grid the rest of the roster uses, and no size or
multiplier here is producible by exactly one pack. A first draft gave this
pack a private off-size rung; measured, one such open named the seat with
certainty, which is the tell the slice exists to remove rather than a way to
differentiate. Personas are separated by WEIGHT — how often each shared size
is taken — and by frequency statistics, never by owning a size.
The bounds are grading rather than taste. A non-blind regular's open stays at
or under 3.0 because `_map_vs_3bet` and `_map_vs_4bet` refuse the whole hand
above `_STD_OPEN_CAP`; both exclude blind openers, which is why the blinds may
go higher. 3-bet rungs stay at or under 3.5, the vs-3-bet cap.
[UNVERIFIED] — the weights. RES-B 4/6.1 sources the LEVELS and confirms the
seat-blind scalars; no committed source gives a distribution of open sizes by
seat at live $2/$3. The ledger
(`docs/ai-dlc/ledger/phase3-derobotization.md`) carries the measured effect,
the roster-level statement about which direction the levels moved, and why.
1.11.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T5, 2026-08-17, second review rework) —
two changes at `cbet_wet`: it gains a 0.33 at 16%, the largest share of the
three regulars because a lag stabs cheap most readily, and it LOSES the 1.5
the previous version added. The share is 16% rather than a third of the
class's requirement because the nit takes none of it — see the nit's 1.9.0
entry, which has the measurement. It costs 7.2% of this pack's wet-flop
bluff mass, which this pack has the room for and the nit does not.
That overbet is withdrawn on both grounds it was granted on. It was fitted:
the smallest weight that cleared the gate it was authored against was 6.86%
and it was set at 8%. And it was weak poker: a flop overbet is a
static-board, nut-advantage tool, and a wet coordinated board is exactly
where correct sizing SHRINKS, because equities run close and the caller
continues wide. The `turn_barrel` overbet stays — turn overbets on scare
cards are a genuine lag habit — so the maniac still shares that cell.
The consequence is disclosed rather than hidden: an overbet on a wet flop is
once again a maniac tell, and the ecology gate carries a named exemption for
it. Realised, P(maniac | a 1.5x bet) is about 0.77 across all nodes.
1.10.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T5, 2026-08-16) — postflop bet sizes are
re-weighted so this seat is no longer identifiable by size alone. The
realised bucket table for the whole roster is in the ticket ledger
(`docs/ai-dlc/ledger/phase3-derobotization.md`) rather than here. The
figures this entry used to carry were wrong in DIRECTION as well as
magnitude — they said the overbet thinned while the same commit was
extending it — which is why they now live in one place, measured once,
with the counting rule stated.
The flat block is deliberately left without one. That block sizes a LEAD, and
an overbet lead is not a lag habit; authoring one to flatten a statistic is
the trade this slice exists to refuse.
`river_value` also gains a 0.33. No regular authored one, so a one-third-pot
river bet identified `station or fish` with probability 1.0. A thin-value or
blocker bet at a third of pot is ordinary for a reg, so this is a realism
gain as much as a tell removal.
Every value stays on the grader's recognised grid {0.33, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0,
1.5}; nothing is jittered continuously.
[UNVERIFIED] — no committed source in this repo gives a population
distribution of bet sizes at low-stakes full ring. See the calling
station's 1.7.0 entry for the one sourced observation this is anchored on.
1.9.0 (de-robotization slice 1, 2026-08-15, review rework) — `vs_rfi`,
`vs_limpers` and the `vs_3bet` OPENER stratum are answered per seat. Facing a
raise, the fold runs 62.62% in the big blind, 73.81% cutoff/button, 75.58%
early and 79.06% in the small blind, against a flat 73.54% before. The big
blind is 1.43x the button by continue rate; the first draft had it at 1.11x.
Two authoring slips found by the range lint were closed at source rather than
inventoried: the late-seat bands played Q9s while folding QJs and 96s while
folding 97s, and AQo 3-bet below the weaker tier beneath it.
[UNVERIFIED] — per-seat defence targets have no committed source; the shape
is judgement, the aggregate it is scaled to is the pre-slice measured value.
1.7.0 (R9-DEFENCE-a T1, 2026-08-02) — ONE new postflop number,
`line_sensitivity`: 0.35 (directional fit seed, tied with passive_fish —
a deliberate tie tier, do not break it). It is READ by
`personas_postflop._line_scaled`, which scales the facing-node CALL and
RAISE merits by `exp(-λ·line)` where `λ = _LINE_DELTA · line_sensitivity`,
so a lag folds more to a persistent hostile line.
1.6.0 (N-LOGIT, 2026-08-02) — ONE new postflop number, `continue_ref`:
0.55, a FROZEN copy of today's effective `call_looseness`. It is the
anchor the facing-node RAISE merit is divided by, so the raise:call odds
stop moving when `call_looseness` is tuned. At the authored value the
ratio is exactly 1.0 and play is bit-identical. NEVER re-sync it with
`call_looseness` — that restores the old coupling and deletes the feature.
1.5.0 (N-LAGWIDTH, 2026-08-01) — one change: the CO, BTN and SB `unopened`
nodes are re-emitted from the same curve spec (now 1.3.0) with an
offsuit-only TRIM (not a swap) at those three seats — the first lag lane
slice to actually reduce width, since the §5 PFR floor argument that held
1.3.0/1.4.0 at constant width does not bind here (owner 2026-08-01
accepted the PFR dip as a disclosed side effect). Suited and pair rows at
CO/BTN/SB are byte-identical to 1.4.0. Combo-weighted %:
Full rationale, per-row edits and the SB J9o preservation constraint: the
N-LAGWIDTH section of content/personas/ladders/lag.unopened.json `_doc`.
The six other seats and every response node (`vs_rfi` / `vs_3bet` /
`vs_4bet`) are untouched — the 1.3.0 opener re-tune below still stands.
1.4.0 (N-LAGCOMP2, 2026-07-31) — one change: the CO, BTN and SB `unopened`
nodes are re-emitted from the same curve spec, again offsuit -> suited and
again a swap rather than a trim, but here EXACTLY width-neutral (the
combo-weighted total is unchanged to the last combo: CO 704.4, BTN 874.8,
SB 687.6 of 1326; pairs untouched at 5.88). The defect: after N-TAGCOMP
fixed the tag's shape, the lag opened a WIDER total range than the tag from
these three seats while covering LESS of the suited universe, i.e. the
loose persona's extra width was offsuit junk.
The suited side is now a class-by-class SUPERSET of the tag's at all three
seats (equal or greater weight on every class the tag opens) and the
offsuit side stays above the tag's, so the roster ordering is preserved on
both axes. Full rationale, the per-row edits and the authoring rule they
obey: the N-LAGCOMP2 section of content/personas/ladders/lag.unopened.json
`_doc` (spec 1.2.0). The six other seats are byte-identical to 1.3.0, and
no response node (`vs_rfi` / `vs_3bet` / `vs_4bet`) was touched — the
1.3.0 opener re-tune below still stands, unmodified.
1.3.0 (N-LAGLADDER, 2026-07-31) — three changes.
(1) All nine `unopened` nodes REPLACED. They are now EMITTED, not
hand-authored: the curve spec is content/personas/ladders/lag.unopened.json
and `python -m tools.rr_emit` regenerates exactly the mixes below (proved
by backend/tests/test_rr_emit.py). This is a COMPOSITION swap at constant
width, NOT a trim — offsuit out, suited in, per seat. ⚠️ THE RIGHT-HAND
SIDE OF EVERY CO / BTN / SB ROW BELOW IS THE 1.3.0 VALUE AND IS NO LONGER
WHAT THIS PACK SHIPS — 1.4.0 above supersedes those three seats (marked
`->1.4.0` inline). The other six seats' figures are current.
Combo-weighted TOTAL moves <=0.36pp at every seat (seat-average 43.15 ->
43.04). The width was deliberately NOT reduced: measured population PFR
sits ON the §5 floor, so a tighten breaches it — see the spec's `_doc`.
Roster ordering tag < lag < maniac still holds at all nine seats, and lag
offsuit width stays above the tag's at every seat.
(2) `vs_rfi` AQo carved out of the 3bet-0.6 mix into {3bet 0.6, call 0.4}
— the fold 0.4 a lag had against a single raise (RR-HOLES T-F3 flagged
row) is now call mass. 3-bet width is unchanged by construction.
(3) `vs_3bet` role=opener, two middle tiers re-tuned: suited-broadway tier
call 0.60->0.55, speculative tier call 0.50->0.46 (fold takes the
difference; 4-bet weights untouched, so the opener 4-bet share stays at
4.00%). Required, not optional: change (1) alone dropped the production
opener fold-to-3-bet to 0.4242 at n=12000, under the [0.43, 0.53] dossier
floor, because a suited-heavier opening range meets a table that folds it
less. Restores 0.4452 @n=12000 vs 0.4534 pre-slice. The role=cold node is
untouched.
